name: Question 1
problem:
Find the general solution of the exact differential equation

$$
2xy\,\text{d}x+({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\text{d}y=0.
$$
worked_solution:
Note that the differential equation is of the form

$$
P(x,y)\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\text{d}y=0
$$

where $P(x,y)=2xy$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.$

Since the equation is exact, our solution $u(x,y)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂u}{∂x}=P(x,y),\,\frac{∂u}{∂y}=Q(x,y)
$$

First, we integrate $P(x,y)$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & =\int 2xy\,\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & ={x}^{2}y+f(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we integrate $Q(x,y)$ with respect to $y.$  Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & =\int {x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & ={x}^{2}y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}+g(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Comparing the two solutions, we see that we must have

$$
g(x)=0,\,f(y)=-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution $u(x,y)=c$ is

$$
{x}^{2}y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}=c.
$$

html:
Question 1
?

Find the general solution of the exact differential equation

2xydx+(x2−y2)dy=0.

a
3x2−y3=c
b
x2−y3=c
c
x2y−y33=c
d
2x2y−y33=c
e
xy−y3=c
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Note that the differential equation is of the form

P(x,y)dx+Q(x,y)dy=0

where P(x,y)=2xy and Q(x,y)=x2−y2.

Since the equation is exact, our solution u(x,y) must satisfy the following system:

∂u∂x=P(x,y),∂u∂y=Q(x,y)

First, we integrate P(x,y) with respect to x. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of y:

u(x,y)=∫P(x,y)dx+f(y)=∫2xydx+f(y)=x2y+f(y)

Next, we integrate Q(x,y) with respect to y. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of x.

u(x,y)=∫Q(x,y)dy+g(x)=∫x2−y2dy+g(x)=x2y−y33+g(x)

Comparing the two solutions, we see that we must have

g(x)=0,f(y)=−y33.

Therefore, the general solution u(x,y)=c is

x2y−y33=c.
